channel.title: Marketing on Best of AI
channel.description: Recent content in Marketing on Best of AI

item.title: BrightEdge
item.description:
BrightEdge targets big websites where SEO is a team effort. Its platform tracks rankings across many keywords and markets, ties organic traffic to revenue, and shows which pages are doing well. Content recommendations point to topics worth writing about and pages to improve, using data on search demand and competitor performance.

AI plays two roles. Inside the platform, machine learning finds patterns and generates recommendations. Outside it, the company tracks how brands appear in AI-generated search results and answer engines, a newer measurement area for marketers. Reporting suits agencies and enterprise teams that must show results to executives.

item.title: BuzzSumo
item.description:
BuzzSumo helps content marketers learn what already works. You enter a topic or domain and see the pieces that earned the most engagement on social networks, along with backlinks, so you can see what resonates before writing. Filters narrow by date, format, and language, which makes it easy to find trending ideas.

Other features cover outreach and monitoring. The influencer search finds people who regularly share and write about a topic, alerts notify you when a keyword or competitor is mentioned, and question tools show what people ask about a subject. AI helps generate ideas and outlines from the findings, and reports can be exported for clients.

item.title: ClickCease
item.description:
ClickCease deals with click fraud in pay-per-click advertising. When advertisers pay for each click on Google or Facebook ads, bots, competitors, and repeated clicks can drain budgets. The tool watches traffic, flags suspicious patterns such as repeated clicks from the same device or location, and adds the offending sources to block lists automatically.

A dashboard shows blocked clicks, estimated savings, and details about where bad traffic came from. Reports can be used to request refunds from ad platforms in some cases. Extras include tracking of invalid traffic on other channels and tools for monitoring ad campaigns and landing pages.

item.title: Creatopy
item.description:
Creatopy is built for ad production. Designers or marketers create a layout in an editor, and the tool adapts it to dozens of banner sizes and social formats, saving the manual resizing that normally eats hours. Animation tools turn static ads into HTML5 banners, and brand kits keep colors, fonts, and logos consistent.

Teams can scale campaigns with a feature that fills templates from a spreadsheet or product feed, producing many variations of an ad automatically. Approval workflows let clients comment and sign off, and integrations push ads directly to ad networks, so there is less downloading and uploading. AI helps with copy, images, and layout suggestions.

item.title: Flourish
item.description:
Flourish makes data storytelling accessible. Users upload a spreadsheet, pick a template such as a bar chart race, scatter plot, hierarchy, map, or scrolling story, and customize colors, labels, and animations. The result is an interactive graphic that can be embedded in a website or article, or exported as an image or video.

Its biggest draw is the library of templates, including formats that are hard to build by hand, like animated race charts and data-driven stories that change as the reader scrolls. Teams can set up brand themes, collaborate on projects, and update charts when data changes. Newsrooms and organizations use it to publish clear graphics quickly.

item.title: Keap
item.description:
Keap targets small service businesses and solo operators. It keeps contacts and conversations in one place, tracks deals through a pipeline, and uses an automation builder to send follow-ups based on what people do, such as filling in a form, opening an email, or paying an invoice. The goal is to keep leads moving without manual chasing.

It also handles the money side. Businesses can send quotes and invoices, take payments, set up recurring billing, and book appointments, which makes it common among coaches, consultants, and home service companies. AI helps draft emails and texts, and templates provide ready-made campaigns.

item.title: Klue
item.description:
Klue is a competitive enablement platform. Product marketing teams gather information on rivals from news, websites, reviews, and internal sales feedback, and organize it into battlecards with talking points, strengths, weaknesses, and objection handling. Sales reps access these cards in their CRM or Slack during deals.

AI helps keep the content fresh. It scans for changes, summarizes updates, and helps draft battlecard sections. Win/loss analysis tools collect feedback from deals and reveal patterns. Reports show which competitive content is used and how it relates to outcomes.

item.title: Mangools
item.description:
Mangools packages the basic SEO jobs in friendly tools. KWFinder finds keywords and shows search volume and difficulty, SERPChecker analyzes the pages ranking for a term, SERPWatcher tracks your rankings over time, LinkMiner shows backlinks, and SiteProfiler gives an overview of a domain. Each is easy to use without deep SEO knowledge.

The strength is simplicity. Color-coded difficulty scores and clean layouts mean beginners can find a keyword worth targeting, and small agencies can report progress to clients. The tools share a login and subscription, and the company offers learning material on SEO basics.

item.title: Mighty Networks
item.description:
Mighty Networks is a platform for building a membership community. A creator sets up a space with feeds, groups, live events, and online courses, and members join by paying a subscription or one-time fee. The pitch is an experience that feels like your own app, with mobile apps that can carry your brand.

Monetization is built in. Creators can charge for memberships, courses, and events, offer tiered access, and run bundles. The AI assistant helps with tasks such as naming a community, drafting posts and course outlines, and suggesting engagement ideas. Analytics show member activity, which helps community managers improve retention.

item.title: MoEngage
item.description:
MoEngage is built for brands with mobile apps and large user bases. It collects behavior data such as app opens, purchases, and browsing, then lets marketers segment users and design campaigns across channels. Journeys can be built visually, so a user who abandons a cart gets a push notification, then an email if they don’t respond.

Analytics show how campaigns perform and how users move through funnels. AI features predict who is likely to churn or buy, choose the best time to send each message, and suggest content, and a generative assistant helps write copy. The platform integrates with data warehouses and other tools, and operates worldwide, with a strong presence in Asia.

item.title: NeuronWriter
item.description:
NeuronWriter is a content optimization tool. A user enters a keyword, the tool analyzes the pages that rank, and it produces a list of recommended terms, questions, and headings, along with a target length. As the writer drafts in its editor, a score shows how well the content covers the topic.

It includes an AI writing assistant for outlines and drafts, internal linking suggestions, and a way to plan content around topics. Competitor analysis shows what top pages do well. Agencies use it for client content because of its pricing.

item.title: Optimizely
item.description:
Optimizely began as an A/B testing tool and grew into a suite for digital experiences. Teams use web experimentation to compare versions of pages, feature experimentation to test changes in apps behind feature flags, and personalization to show different content to different audiences. Statistical engines determine which variations win, and rollouts can be controlled to reduce risk.

The platform also includes content management and commerce. A CMS lets marketers create and manage web content, and commerce products support B2B and B2C stores, so a company can build, publish, test, and optimize in a single environment. AI features, under the Opal brand, help generate content, suggest experiment ideas, and run agents that automate steps in marketing workflows.

item.title: Postscript
item.description:
Postscript focuses on text message marketing for online stores. It connects to Shopify, collects subscribers through popups and checkout opt-ins, and lets merchants send campaigns about sales and product launches. Automated flows trigger messages for events like abandoned carts, browse behavior, and order updates, which tend to produce strong results.

Segmentation uses shopping data, such as purchase history and product interest, to tailor messages. Two-way conversations let customers reply and get help from a team member, and an AI assistant helps draft messages and suggests offers. Analytics tie texts to revenue so merchants can see what pays off.

item.title: Skool
item.description:
Skool is a simple platform for running a community. Members post in a feed, take courses in a classroom section, attend events from a shared calendar, and earn points for participating, which unlock levels on a leaderboard. The gamification is meant to keep people engaged without a lot of setup.

The pricing and design are deliberately simple. Skool charges a flat fee for community owners and offers few customization options, so creators spend time on content and members, not on configuring a site. Communities can charge a monthly or annual fee, and a built-in discovery page, plus members’ direct messages, helps people find groups.

item.title: SpyFu
item.description:
SpyFu is a competitor research tool. Enter a domain and it reveals the keywords that site ranks for in organic search, the keywords it buys on Google Ads, and how those change over time. The ad history is a distinctive feature, since you can see which ad copy a competitor has tested and kept running.

That data helps marketers decide where to compete. Keyword research shows search volume and difficulty, backlink tools find link opportunities, and rank tracking monitors progress. Agencies use the reports to pitch clients, and PPC managers use the ad history to find ideas and gaps in their own campaigns.

item.title: Storylane
item.description:
Storylane is an interactive demo platform. A user records their product with a browser extension that captures screenshots or the underlying page, then adds hotspots, tooltips, and callouts to guide viewers through a story. The result is a demo that prospects can click through on their own, without needing a sandbox or a live call.

Teams use it across the sales cycle. Marketing embeds demos on landing pages, sales sends personalized versions in outreach emails, and customer success uses them for onboarding. AI features add voiceovers, translations into other languages, and personalization of names and logos for each prospect. Analytics show who viewed a demo and where they dropped off.

item.title: Syte
item.description:
Syte brings visual search to e-commerce. A shopper uploads a photo or taps on an image, and the system finds similar items in the store’s catalog. Computer vision also tags products with detailed attributes, which improves search, filters, and recommendations.

Retailers use it for shop-the-look features, similar item suggestions, and personalization. Integrations work with common e-commerce platforms, and generative AI supports conversational shopping assistants.

Syte is sold to retailers on subscription. Alternatives include Algolia, Bloomreach, Vue.ai, Klevu, and Google Lens integrations. Syte suits fashion and home retailers with large catalogs.

item.title: TubeBuddy
item.description:
TubeBuddy is a browser extension and mobile app for YouTube creators. It adds tools to the YouTube interface, including a keyword explorer that estimates how competitive a search term is, tag suggestions, and a score that shows how well a video is optimized. These help creators choose topics and fill in titles and descriptions with search in mind.

Other features save time. Bulk tools update many videos at once, thumbnail A/B testing compares designs for click rates, and scheduling and reminders organize publishing. Analytics show how a channel performs and how it compares to others. AI tools suggest titles, descriptions, and ideas based on a video’s topic.

item.title: marketingskills
item.description:
This repository bundles the following skills:

  • product-marketing: Foundational skill that other marketing skills check first for shared context.
  • cro: Covers conversion rate optimization workflows.
  • copywriting: Provides guidance for writing marketing copy.
  • seo-audit: Runs an SEO audit of a site.
  • ai-seo: Optimizes content for AI-driven search and discovery.
  • programmatic-seo: Builds programmatic SEO pages at scale.
  • ab-testing: Sets up and analyzes A/B tests.
  • analytics: Covers analytics setup and interpretation.
  • churn-prevention: Identifies and addresses customer churn.
  • referrals: Builds referral and growth loops.
  • pricing: Provides guidance on pricing strategy.
  • launch: Coordinates product launch workflows.
  • cold-email: Drafts cold outreach emails.

item.title: Circle
item.description:
Circle gives communities a home of their own. A creator sets up spaces for topics, posts content, hosts live events, runs courses, and lets members message each other, all under a custom domain and brand. It aims to feel more focused than a social network and less cluttered than a forum.

Monetization is built in. Communities can charge for memberships, offer paid tiers, and sell courses and events, with workflows to onboard new members. AI features draft welcome messages, summarize conversations, and help members find information, while analytics show engagement and which members are most active. Mobile apps and integrations with tools like Zapier extend reach.

item.title: NationBuilder
item.description:
NationBuilder is designed for people building a movement. A campaign or organization keeps records of supporters, volunteers, and donors in one database, runs a website, sends email and texts, organizes events, and takes donations. Having everything together helps small teams manage a large network.

Tools support organizing, such as lists, tags, and tasks for volunteers, and reporting on progress toward goals. AI features help draft messages and summarize supporter information. The platform is used by campaigns, community groups, and associations around the world.

item.title: VidIQ
item.description:
vidIQ helps YouTubers grow. A browser extension adds data to YouTube pages and Studio, showing keyword scores, competitor stats, and tags used by successful videos. Research tools find topics with demand and low competition.

AI features suggest video ideas, titles, and thumbnails, write descriptions, and give feedback on videos. Analytics track subscriber growth and performance, and a coach feature gives guidance.

vidIQ has a free plan and paid tiers. Optimization scores are guides, and content quality drives results. Alternatives include TubeBuddy, Morningfame, Social Blade, and YouTube’s own research tools. vidIQ suits creators optimizing a channel.

item.title: Igly
item.description:
Igly focuses on product images. A seller uploads photos of items, and the tool removes or replaces backgrounds, places products in lifestyle scenes, adjusts lighting, and creates variations for marketplaces. An infinite canvas lets users arrange and edit many images in one project.

Agents handle multi-step edits from a plain description, such as producing a set of listing images in a consistent style. Presets match the dimensions and rules of common platforms. Sellers use it to reduce the cost of photography and design.

item.title: Alli AI
item.description:
Alli AI addresses a common obstacle in SEO: implementing recommended changes often requires developer time. Alli installs a snippet on a website, and then SEO teams can edit and push on-page elements, such as titles, meta descriptions, headings, schema markup, and internal links, directly from its dashboard to many pages at once. Changes can be tested and rolled back, and the platform tracks results.

AI features suggest optimizations. The tool analyzes pages and recommends improvements, can generate titles and descriptions in bulk, and automates tasks such as adding structured data. Agencies value it for managing many client sites through one interface, and enterprises use it to speed up large-scale optimization where release cycles are slow.

item.title: Arcade
item.description:
Arcade makes interactive demos simple to create. A person records their screen using a Chrome extension, and Arcade turns the clicks into a step-by-step walkthrough with highlights and captions. The result can be edited, branded, and shared as a link or embedded on a website or in an email.

Teams use demos for several purposes. Marketing places them on landing pages to show a product in action, sales sends them to prospects, and customer success uses them for onboarding and help content. AI features add voiceovers, generate captions, and personalize demos by changing names and details. Analytics show who watched and where they stopped.

item.title: Cognism
item.description:
Cognism helps salespeople reach the right people. Its database covers companies and contacts across regions, with a reputation for strong coverage in Europe and for verified mobile numbers, which are valuable for cold calling. Users filter by role, industry, size, and technology, then export or sync contacts to their CRM.

Intent data adds timing. Signals show which accounts are researching topics related to a product, so teams can prioritize outreach. Compliance is a selling point: the company screens contacts against do-not-call lists and says it follows privacy rules like GDPR, which matters for outreach in Europe.

item.title: Instapage
item.description:
Instapage focuses on the page that visitors reach after clicking an ad. Marketers build pages in a drag-and-drop editor with templates, connect them to ad campaigns, and track conversion rates. Collaboration features let teams and clients comment directly on designs.

Optimization tools set it apart. A/B testing compares versions, heatmaps show where visitors engage, and personalization changes page content depending on the ad or audience that sent the visitor. AI helps write copy and suggests improvements.

item.title: Kaspr
item.description:
Kaspr is a contact data tool for outbound sales. While browsing a LinkedIn profile, a user clicks the Kaspr extension to reveal a professional email address and phone number, then saves the contact to a CRM or a list. It also supports bulk searches and enrichment of existing records.

The company emphasizes European data and compliance with privacy rules like GDPR, and offers ways for individuals to opt out of the database. Credits limit how many contact details a user can reveal each month, and integrations connect with CRMs and sales engagement tools.

item.title: Keyword Insights
item.description:
Keyword Insights helps turn a long keyword list into a content plan. A user uploads thousands of keywords or discovers them in the tool, and the platform clusters them based on how search results overlap, which indicates whether a group of terms should be targeted by one page or several.

It also determines search intent for each cluster, suggests content types, and produces briefs that outline what a page should cover based on top results. Rank tracking and content tools support the workflow after publishing, and AI assists with drafting.

item.title: Lusha
item.description:
Lusha helps sales and recruiting teams get in touch with prospects. While viewing a profile on LinkedIn or a company website, a user clicks the Lusha extension to reveal contact information, then saves it to a CRM. A database search finds contacts by role, company size, and industry.

Additional features include intent signals, technology data, and enrichment of existing lists, as well as integrations with Salesforce, HubSpot, and sales engagement tools. The company emphasizes compliance with privacy laws and offers ways for people to opt out.

item.title: Navattic
item.description:
Navattic helps companies show software without a live demo. A marketer captures a product’s screens or pages, adds callouts and steps, and publishes a tour that visitors can click through. Gated or ungated, these demos let prospects see the product before talking to sales.

Analytics show who viewed a demo and how far they went, giving sales a signal about interest. Personalization lets teams tailor tours by account, and integrations send engagement data to CRMs and marketing tools. AI helps create and edit demos and write copy.

item.title: Phrasee
item.description:
Phrasee focuses on the words in marketing messages. A team sets up a brand voice, and the platform generates many variations of subject lines, push text, or ads, predicts which will perform best, and tests them against audiences. Results feed back to improve future suggestions.

The company has become part of Jacquard Group, which combines it with other brand messaging tools. Large retailers, financial institutions, and travel brands used it to squeeze more from large campaigns, where small improvements in open rate add up.

item.title: Planable
item.description:
Planable is built around approval workflows. Marketers create posts in a view that looks like the final social post, share it with teammates or clients, collect comments and approvals, and schedule it once signed off. This replaces long email chains and screenshots.

Features include a content calendar, multiple approval stages, and support for many networks. AI tools help draft captions and ideas. Agencies find it useful for client work where sign-off is required.

item.title: Seamless AI
item.description:
Seamless.AI helps salespeople find who to contact. Users search by title, industry, and location, or use a browser extension to look up contacts on websites, and the platform returns emails and phone numbers pulled from public sources and its database. Lists export to CRMs and engagement tools.

Real-time search and enrichment aim to keep data fresh, and intent signals show which accounts may be in a buying cycle. AI features help write outreach and prioritize accounts.

item.title: Sprinklr
item.description:
Sprinklr serves very large organizations. It manages publishing across social channels, listens for brand mentions, handles customer care across messaging and voice, and analyzes market trends, using a shared data layer so teams see the whole customer picture.

AI runs through the platform: models classify conversations, detect sentiment, route cases, suggest replies, and generate content, and agents handle some customer interactions. Governance tools suit regulated industries and large teams.

Sprinklr is sold on enterprise subscriptions, with high cost and complexity. Alternatives include Hootsuite, Sprout Social, Khoros, Emplifi, and Salesforce. Sprinklr suits large brands managing many channels.

item.title: Supademo
item.description:
Supademo makes product demos quickly. A user records clicks through an app with a browser extension, and Supademo converts them into a step-by-step interactive demo with callouts, which can be edited, branded, and embedded on a site or emailed.

AI adds voiceover narration and translations, and helps write step text. Analytics show who viewed a demo and where they stopped. The tool is also used for onboarding guides and help documentation.

item.title: Typeform
item.description:
Typeform changed the feel of online forms. Instead of showing a long page of fields, it presents one question at a time with large type and smooth transitions, which tends to make forms feel friendlier and often improves completion rates. People use it for surveys, quizzes, lead capture, registrations, feedback, and onboarding. Design options and templates make it easy to match a brand.

Behind the interface are capable features. Logic jumps change the next question based on earlier answers, calculators and scoring support quizzes, payments can be collected, and files can be uploaded. Integrations send responses to tools like Google Sheets, HubSpot, Slack, and Zapier. AI features help generate a form from a short prompt, suggest questions, and summarize responses so teams can understand results faster.

item.title: Writecream
item.description:
Writecream offers many small tools in one place. Users generate cold emails with personalized openers based on a prospect’s profile, write blog posts and ad copy, create images, and clone voices or make avatar videos.

Its outreach features appeal to sales teams that want personalization at scale, such as icebreakers for LinkedIn or email. Other tools cover general content needs.

Writecream has a free tier and paid plans. Generic AI personalization can feel obvious to recipients, and outreach must follow spam and privacy law. Alternatives include Lemlist, Copy.ai, Jasper, Instantly, and Clay. Writecream suits small teams wanting varied content tools.

item.title: Datawrapper
item.description:
Datawrapper was built by journalists for journalists. A user pastes or uploads data, chooses a chart type such as a bar, line, scatter plot, or map, and adjusts labels, colors, and annotations. The result is a responsive graphic that works on phones and desktops, and can be embedded in a story or exported as an image.

Its design defaults follow good data visualization practice, so charts look clear without fiddling. Features include color-blind friendly palettes, tables with inline bars, locator maps, and a way to update charts automatically from a linked data source. News organizations around the world use it, and teams can share themes to keep a consistent style.

item.title: Catchlight
item.description:
Catchlight is a lead scoring tool for financial advisory firms. It enriches a prospect’s profile with data such as estimated income, investable assets, age range, and interests, then applies a model trained on past conversions to produce a score showing how likely they are to become a client.

Advisors use it to prioritize their time. Instead of calling every inquiry, they can focus on those with the best fit, and see context to start a conversation. It integrates with CRMs used by advisors, such as Wealthbox, and appears in platforms that serve wealth management firms.

item.title: 6sense
item.description:
6sense helps B2B teams find buyers who are not yet raising their hands. It collects signals from many sources, such as web visits, content consumption, and third-party research activity, identifies the companies behind the anonymous traffic, and uses machine learning to predict which accounts are in the market and at what stage of the buying journey. Teams see lists of target accounts ranked by readiness to buy.

The platform acts on those insights. Marketing can run advertising aimed at accounts showing interest, sales gets alerts when key accounts spike in activity, and workflows enroll contacts in email sequences. AI agents help with outreach and qualification, and integrations with CRMs and marketing automation tools keep data in sync. Predictions rely on data from many sources, so they are probabilistic.

item.title: AdCreative.ai
item.description:
AdCreative.ai is aimed at marketers who need many ad variations quickly. You enter your brand colors, logo, and product details, and it produces sets of banners and social ads in different sizes, along with headlines and body text. Instead of starting from a blank canvas, you choose from designs and tweak them. That volume is useful for testing, since ad performance often depends on trying many variations.

What sets it apart is scoring. A creative score estimates how well each design is likely to perform, based on models trained on ad performance data, and insights tools suggest what to change. If you connect your ad accounts, the system can learn which visuals and copy work for your audience, and competitor insights show what rivals are running. Newer features add product photoshoots and user-generated-style videos made by AI.

item.title: Ahrefs
item.description: Ahrefs is best known for its backlink data. Its crawler maps links across the web, so you can look at any site and see who links to it, which pages draw the most traffic, and what keywords bring visitors. Site Explorer is the tool most people open first, and it is often used to study a competitor’s strategy. Keywords Explorer suggests search terms and estimates how hard each one would be to rank for.

item.title: Anyword
item.description:
Anyword’s distinguishing feature is its performance prediction. When you ask for ad copy or an email subject line, the platform generates several versions and gives each a predicted score, based on models trained on large amounts of marketing performance data, along with an estimate for different audiences. The idea is to help marketers choose which copy to test or publish instead of guessing.

It works across typical marketing needs: ad copy for social and search, email campaigns, landing pages, blog content, and product descriptions. Brand voice settings and a knowledge base keep outputs consistent with a company’s tone and facts. Teams can integrate it with ad platforms and other tools, and an analytics layer connects the predictions with actual results. Targeting options adapt copy to specific audience segments.

item.title: Apollo
item.description:
Apollo gives sales teams a place to find and contact prospects. Users search a database of people and companies by title, industry, size, and technology used, then add leads to email sequences, calling lists, and LinkedIn tasks. A browser extension finds contact details as you browse the web.

The platform includes tools for the whole outbound workflow: email verification, scheduling, a dialer, meeting booking, analytics, and integrations with CRMs like Salesforce and HubSpot. AI features help write messages, score leads, and automate steps, and workflows can enrich existing records to keep a CRM current.

item.title: Attentive
item.description:
Attentive helps brands market over text message. Shoppers opt in through signup forms and popups, and the brand sends campaigns, product alerts, and automated messages such as abandoned cart reminders and back-in-stock notices. Messages can include images and links, and customers can reply to start a conversation.

AI plays a part in targeting and content. The platform chooses send times, predicts which offers each subscriber might respond to, and helps write messages in a brand’s voice. Integrations with Shopify, Klaviyo, and other tools bring in purchase data, and analytics tie messages to revenue. A service team often helps brands set up programs.

item.title: BigCommerce
item.description:
BigCommerce provides the pieces needed to sell online. A merchant sets up a storefront with themes, manages products and inventory, accepts payments, calculates shipping and tax, and sells across channels such as Amazon, eBay, Google, social platforms, and marketplaces. Many features that other platforms handle through apps, such as product variants, reviews, and discounts, are built in, which keeps costs more predictable.

It stands out in two areas. It supports B2B commerce with features like customer-specific pricing, quotes, and bulk ordering, and it’s designed for headless setups in which the storefront is built separately and connected through APIs, which suits brands wanting a custom front end. AI tools help generate product descriptions, support merchandising, and optimize search, and an ecosystem of apps and partners extends the platform.

item.title: Buffer
item.description: Buffer is built for people who want to run their social accounts without living in each app. You connect your profiles, write a post once, adjust it per platform, and schedule it into a queue that publishes at set times. A calendar view shows what is planned, and an idea library keeps drafts and inspiration in one place. The interface is deliberately plain, which is a big part of why freelancers, creators, and small businesses like it.

item.title: Canva
item.description: For infographics, Canva works as a template-first editor. You choose a layout for a process, timeline, comparison, statistic, or report, then replace the placeholder text and swap in your own colors and fonts. The element library supplies icons, illustrations, shapes, and photos, and chart tools let you paste or upload numbers to draw bar charts, pie charts, and other graphs that update when the data changes. Because it is a drag-and-drop tool, people without design training can produce something tidy in under an hour.

item.title: ContentStudio
item.description:
ContentStudio combines content discovery, creation, and publishing. Users find trending topics and articles, curate and share them, write posts with an AI assistant, and schedule to networks such as Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, X, TikTok, and WordPress blogs. A calendar shows what is planned across channels.

Features for teams and agencies include approval workflows, client management, white-label reports, and analytics on performance. The AI writer generates captions, hashtags, and blog drafts, and image tools help create visuals. Social inbox features centralize replies and comments.

item.title: Conversica
item.description:
Conversica automates the follow-up that sales teams often drop. When a lead comes in, the AI assistant sends personalized messages, reads replies, answers questions, and tries to book a meeting. If a prospect does not respond, it continues with a sequence of nudges, which keeps leads from going cold.

The assistants are used in industries such as automotive, education, software, and financial services, where large volumes of inquiries arrive. Conversation data flows into the CRM, so salespeople see which leads are qualified and what was said. The company has added generative AI to make conversations more natural.

item.title: Copy.ai
item.description:
Copy.ai began as one of the first popular AI copywriting tools. Users choose a template or write a prompt, and the tool generates headlines, product descriptions, email sequences, ads, and social captions. A brand voice feature helps keep the tone consistent.

The product later shifted toward workflows for go-to-market teams. Marketers and sales teams can chain steps that research accounts, draft outreach, and produce content at scale, using multiple language models. Chat and knowledge features let the AI draw on company information.

item.title: Demandbase
item.description:
Demandbase focuses on selling to companies rather than individuals. It builds a view of target accounts from first-party and third-party data, including website visits, content use, and intent signals showing which accounts are researching a topic. Marketing and sales teams see which accounts are heating up and who within them is involved.

The platform acts on those signals. Advertising features serve targeted ads to the buying committee at chosen accounts, sales tools alert reps when accounts show interest, and orchestration coordinates campaigns across channels. AI helps score accounts, predict fit, and recommend actions, and an assistant answers questions about account data.

item.title: Dynamic Yield
item.description:
Dynamic Yield helps businesses show each customer the content most likely to interest them. It collects behavior data from web, mobile, and email channels, builds profiles and segments, and uses machine learning to choose which products, banners, or messages to show. Retailers use it for recommendations like customers also bought, personalized homepages, and tailored promotions.

The platform also covers testing and optimization. Teams run experiments to compare versions of pages, with statistics to determine winners, and use triggers such as exit intent to present timely offers. Integrations connect with e-commerce platforms, customer data platforms, and marketing tools, and AI features suggest audiences and automate decisions. It supports use in industries including retail, travel, banking, and media.

item.title: Flick AI
item.description:
Flick targets people who manage social media without a large team. It combines content planning with AI writing: you can brainstorm ideas, generate captions and post drafts in your own style, and organize them on a calendar before scheduling. A hashtag tool suggests relevant tags, and an analytics view helps you see what performs well.

An AI assistant trained on your past content tries to match your tone and topics, so drafts need less editing than generic output. The platform supports multiple networks, including Instagram, LinkedIn, and TikTok, and offers collaboration features for agencies or small teams to review and approve content. Prompts and templates help with common formats such as carousels and short videos.

item.title: Frase
item.description:
Frase helps content teams plan and write articles that can rank. Enter a keyword, and Frase analyzes the top search results to show the topics, questions, and headings they cover and the terms they use, then creates a brief that guides a writer. As you draft, a score shows how well your article covers the topic compared with competitors, and suggestions help fill gaps.

AI features support writing and optimization. Frase can generate outlines and drafts, answer questions drawn from search data, and update existing articles to improve their performance. Newer tools track visibility in AI-generated answers from assistants and search engines, reflecting the shift in how people find information, and an agent can handle parts of the content workflow. Integrations with Google Search Console and publishing tools connect data to action.

item.title: GrowthBar
item.description:
GrowthBar tries to simplify SEO for people who are not specialists. You enter a keyword, and the tool shows search volume and difficulty, related keywords, and what the top-ranking pages cover, including their headings and word counts. A Chrome extension displays similar data directly in search results, which helps when researching competitors.

The AI content features turn that research into drafts. GrowthBar can generate outlines, blog posts, and meta descriptions, and tools for rewriting and expanding text help refine them. It also includes rank tracking and backlink data, and an AI assistant to help brainstorm topics. The target users are small business owners, freelancers, and agencies that publish content regularly.

item.title: Hootsuite
item.description:
Hootsuite is one of the oldest social media management tools. Teams connect accounts for networks such as Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, X, TikTok, and YouTube, plan content on a calendar, schedule posts, and respond to comments and messages in a shared inbox. Approval workflows suit larger organizations.

Listening and analytics tools track brand mentions and compare performance across channels. OwlyWriter, the AI assistant, helps write captions, suggest ideas, and repurpose content. Advertising management and employee advocacy products extend the suite for enterprises.

item.title: HubSpot
item.description: HubSpot began as an inbound marketing tool, and Marketing Hub is still the center of its original idea: attract visitors with useful content, capture them as contacts, and nurture them toward a purchase. It includes email marketing, landing pages, forms, blogging, social publishing, ad tracking, and SEO recommendations, all tied to a CRM that records every interaction with a contact. That shared data is what lets a marketer see which campaigns produce actual customers, not only clicks.

item.title: Hunter
item.description: Hunter is a tool for finding contact details for business outreach. A Domain Search shows the email addresses associated with a company along with the sources where they were found, and the email pattern the company uses. An Email Finder takes a person’s name and company and returns the most likely address with a confidence score. Email Verifier checks whether an address is valid and likely to deliver, which reduces bounces.

item.title: Hypotenuse AI
item.description:
Hypotenuse AI is built for online stores with large catalogs. You upload a spreadsheet of products with attributes, and it writes descriptions for each one, in a consistent tone and optimized for search, saving the effort of writing hundreds or thousands of descriptions by hand. It can also produce category pages, meta descriptions, blog posts, and ad copy.

Features support brand and workflow. A brand voice setting keeps text aligned with a company’s style, a plagiarism check helps ensure uniqueness, and integrations connect with Shopify and other platforms to publish content directly. The product also offers AI image tools for creating and editing product images and backgrounds, which makes it a toolkit for content across a catalog.

item.title: Infogram
item.description:
Infogram helps turn numbers into visual stories. You choose a template for an infographic, report, chart, or dashboard, import data from a spreadsheet or connect to a live source, and customize the design with your brand colors and fonts. The tool produces polished charts and maps, many of them interactive, that can be embedded on websites or shared as links.

Several features support data communication. Over thirty chart types, including maps and tables, handle different kinds of data, and live data connections update visuals when the source changes. Teams can collaborate on projects, keep brand templates, and publish with analytics. Downloads include images and PDFs, and AI features help generate visuals and suggest ways to present data.

item.title: Jasper
item.description:
For copywriting, Jasper offers more structure than a general chatbot. Marketers choose a format such as a Facebook ad, a product description, a landing page section, or an email sequence, supply the details, and get multiple options in their brand’s voice. The Brand Voice feature learns tone and style from examples, and a company knowledge base provides facts about products and audiences so the copy uses accurate claims.

Collaboration features suit teams. Shared templates and style guides keep writers consistent, and campaigns can be planned in one place with copy, images, and variations for different channels. An editor helps refine text, change tone, and check for plagiarism. Newer agent features help automate common marketing tasks, such as producing a set of assets from a brief.

item.title: Jasper
item.description:
As a marketing platform, Jasper aims to speed up the full path from a brief to a finished campaign. Marketers define their brand voice, audience, and product information once, then generate blog posts, social posts, ads, emails, and landing pages that follow those guidelines. Campaign tools help plan content around a launch, adapt messages for each channel, and keep versions organized.

The latest versions emphasize agents and workflows. Specialized agents handle tasks such as researching a topic, creating a content calendar, repurposing a webinar into several assets, and optimizing copy for search. Integrations connect with tools such as Google Docs, Webflow, and HubSpot, and analytics features tie content to performance. Controls let enterprises govern who can use what and ensure compliance with brand rules.

item.title: Later
item.description:
Later started as a way to plan Instagram feeds visually. Users drag photos and videos onto a calendar, see how the grid will look, write captions, and schedule posts to go out automatically. It has since expanded to other networks, including TikTok, Pinterest, LinkedIn, Facebook, and X, with tools to manage a content library, collaborate with teammates, and track results.

Other features support social growth. A link-in-bio page lets creators send followers to multiple destinations, analytics show which posts perform best and when audiences are most active, and AI helps write captions, suggest hashtags, and repurpose content. The company also owns an influencer marketing platform, which helps brands find creators and manage campaigns.

item.title: LinkedIn Sales Navigator
item.description:
Sales Navigator gives salespeople deeper access to LinkedIn’s network. It provides advanced filters for finding people and companies, such as by seniority, function, company size, industry, and recent job changes. Users save leads and accounts into lists, and the system sends alerts when something relevant happens, like a prospect changing jobs or a company hiring in a certain department, which can prompt a timely message.

Further features support outreach. InMail messages reach people outside your network, TeamLink shows how colleagues are connected to a prospect for warm introductions, and integrations sync with CRMs such as Salesforce and HubSpot to keep records current. AI tools recommend leads, summarize accounts, and suggest ways to start a conversation, using the profile and activity data on the platform.

item.title: Magento
item.description:
Magento was created as an open-source e-commerce framework and became one of the most customizable platforms for online stores. Merchants with complex needs use it to manage large catalogs, multiple storefronts and currencies, custom pricing and checkout, and integrations with ERP and other systems. A huge ecosystem of extensions, agencies, and developers supports it.

Adobe acquired Magento and sells a commercial version, Adobe Commerce, with additional features for B2B selling, merchandising, and cloud hosting and support, plus integration with Adobe’s marketing and analytics products. Adobe Sensei AI powers features such as product recommendations and search. The free Magento Open Source edition continues for those who want to host and manage their own stores.

item.title: MarketMuse
item.description:
MarketMuse approaches content from the perspective of topical authority. It scans your website and compares the topics you cover with what search engines expect from a site in your area, then shows gaps where new or improved content could help. Instead of focusing on single keywords, it helps plan clusters of related articles that together establish expertise.

Its tools turn that strategy into work. Content briefs list the subtopics, questions, and terms a piece should address, an optimization tool scores drafts against those expectations, and AI helps with drafting and updating existing pages. Metrics such as personalized difficulty estimate how hard a topic will be for your site specifically. Teams use the platform to prioritize where to invest effort.

item.title: Metricool
item.description:
Metricool brings several marketing tasks into one dashboard. Users can plan and schedule posts across networks on a calendar, see analytics on posts, followers, and competitors, and manage Facebook, Instagram, Google, and TikTok ads reports. A link-in-bio tool, inbox for comments and messages, and web analytics help connect social activity to site traffic.

Reporting is a strong point. Customizable reports can be exported or scheduled for clients, and integrations connect with Looker Studio and other business intelligence tools, which suits agencies. AI features help write captions, suggest posting times, and generate content ideas, and a feature can plan a calendar from a brief. Plans cover multiple brands, so one account can manage several clients.

item.title: Missinglettr
item.description:
Missinglettr automates a task many content creators neglect: promoting their articles over time. You connect your blog or paste a link, and the tool analyzes the post to pull out quotes, statistics, and highlights. It then generates a series of social posts, with images, scheduled across weeks and months, so a single article continues to attract visitors long after it’s published.

Other features round out the platform. A curation tool suggests relevant content from other sources to share, a social media scheduler handles regular posting, and analytics show engagement. Collaboration features allow agencies and teams to manage several brands. AI helps with writing captions and variations, and automated hashtag suggestions save time.

item.title: Moz Pro
item.description:
Moz was one of the earliest SEO software companies, and Moz Pro remains a staple for agencies and in-house marketers. Users research keywords, audit sites for technical problems, track rankings over time, and analyze links, with Domain Authority, Moz’s well-known score, used as a quick measure of a site’s strength.

The MozBar browser extension overlays metrics on search results and web pages, making competitor checks quick. Reporting tools produce client-ready summaries, and newer AI features suggest priorities and help with content. A separate local product manages business listings.

item.title: NeuralText
item.description:
NeuralText is an SEO content suite. Users find keywords, group them into clusters by intent, study what ranks for a term, and create content briefs that list topics and questions to cover. The AI writer then drafts articles or sections using those guidelines.

The tool aims to let one person handle research, planning, and drafting. A content editor scores text against the brief, and additional templates cover ads, product descriptions, and social posts.

item.title: Nosto
item.description:
Nosto helps online stores treat every visitor differently. It tracks browsing and purchase behavior and uses it to recommend products, order category pages, personalize search, and show targeted messages. Merchants configure these experiences with a visual tool and rules, and the system learns what works.

Features include product recommendations across the site and in emails, a search engine that understands intent, and tools to personalize content by audience. Shopify, Magento, and other platforms are supported. Generative AI helps write product copy and campaign content.

item.title: Okendo
item.description:
Okendo helps online stores build trust with reviews. After a purchase, it asks customers for reviews with photos and video, displays them on product pages, and syndicates them to Google. Surveys and attributes gather more detail about the customer and product fit.

Additional tools include a loyalty and referral program and a customer data layer. AI summarizes reviews into themes, analyzes sentiment, and suggests replies, helping merchants learn what customers like and dislike. Integrations connect with email, helpdesk, and ads tools.

item.title: Pattern89
item.description:
Pattern89 set out to bring data to creative decisions. Advertisers produce many images and videos but often cannot tell which elements drive results. The platform analyzed an advertiser’s past ads and performance data, tagging the visual and text elements in each, such as colors, faces, products, and calls to action, and learned which combinations worked for a given audience and channel.

With that knowledge, it could score new creative before launch and suggest changes, and recommend which assets to prioritize. Marketers used it to reduce wasted spend on ads that were unlikely to work, and to give designers concrete guidance. Integrations with social ad platforms pulled in performance data.

item.title: Pencil
item.description:
Pencil helps marketing teams produce a steady stream of ads. You connect your brand assets and product information, and Pencil generates video and image ads with copy and voiceovers in different formats for platforms like Meta, TikTok, and YouTube. Teams can create many variations, which makes testing easier than designing each ad by hand.

The prediction layer is the distinctive part. Pencil scores creative on how likely it is to perform, using models trained on a large amount of ad performance data and refined with the account’s own results. It also helps track which messages and visuals win and feeds that back into the next round of creative. Integrations with ad platforms and Shopify bring in performance data and product catalogs.

item.title: Peppertype.ai
item.description:
Peppertype.ai started as a copywriting assistant and has grown into a broader content tool for marketers. Users pick a type of content, such as an ad, a product description, a blog outline, or a LinkedIn post, supply the topic and tone, and receive several drafts. Brand voice and knowledge settings help it reflect a company’s style, and templates cover many common marketing formats.

It is part of Pepper Content, a company that also runs a marketplace of freelance writers and managed content services, which is the source of the Peppertype name. That connection lets teams combine AI drafting with human writers and editors for higher-stakes content. Workflow tools support collaboration, review, and publishing, and the platform has added AI agents for tasks like research and repurposing content.

item.title: Persado
item.description:
Persado focuses on the specific words in marketing messages. Its premise is that the choice of language, including emotions, calls to action, and phrasing, affects whether people respond, and that machine learning can learn what works. Marketers give it a campaign goal and brand guidelines, and it generates message variations and predicts which will perform best, based on its library of language and results from past campaigns.

Large brands in finance, retail, and telecommunications use Persado to optimize email subject lines, ads, and push notifications at scale. It integrates with marketing platforms, tests variants, and learns from the results to improve future messages. More recently, the company has added generative AI tools for drafting and personalizing content within brand guardrails.

item.title: Piktochart
item.description: Piktochart is aimed at people who need to present information visually but are not designers. You choose a template for an infographic, report, presentation, or poster, edit the text and images, and add charts and maps that you can link to data. Visual blocks, icons, illustrations, and a library of graphics make it quick to produce clean results, and the tool exports to image and PDF formats or shares online.

item.title: Privy
item.description:
Privy gives small stores a way to capture and convert visitors. Pop-ups and banners collect emails and texts with offers, automated emails recover abandoned carts, and campaigns promote products to subscribers. Everything runs from one dashboard connected to the store.

AI assists with writing and targeting, such as drafting emails and choosing segments. Templates and recipes simplify setup for merchants without a marketing team, and analytics show revenue from each campaign.

item.title: Recharge
item.description:
Recharge enables subscribe-and-save models for online stores. Merchants on Shopify and other platforms set up subscription products, let customers manage deliveries and payments in a portal, and bill on schedule. It is common in consumables such as food, supplements, and beauty products.

Analytics show retention, churn, and revenue, and tools help reduce cancellations. Smart payment retries recover failed charges, and AI models predict which subscribers may leave so merchants can intervene with offers or pauses.

item.title: SEMrush
item.description: Semrush is among the most widely used toolkits for search marketers. Its core is a big database of keywords and domains, so you can see which terms a competitor ranks for, how much traffic a page gets, who links to it, and where your own site stands. Keyword research, position tracking, site audits, and backlink analysis cover the regular work of search optimization. Separate tools handle paid search, content planning, local listings, and social media.

item.title: Shopify
item.description: Shopify lets someone start an online store without building the software behind it. You choose a theme, add products, set up payments and shipping, and the platform handles hosting, the checkout, and tax and currency settings. The same system also covers in-person sales through point-of-sale hardware, so a shop can manage online and physical inventory together. Everything from a one-person side business to large brands runs on it, and Shop Pay, its accelerated checkout, is used well beyond Shopify’s own stores.

item.title: Smartly.io
item.description:
Smartly, formerly Smartly.io, serves brands and agencies that run large ad programs. Its platform connects to major social networks and lets teams build and launch many campaigns from one interface, apply rules, and update thousands of ads at once. For retailers with big catalogs, dynamic ads are generated automatically from product feeds, adjusting to inventory and price.

The product emphasizes creative and optimization. Creative automation produces many ad variations in different sizes and languages from templates, which helps with testing and localization. Predictive budget allocation shifts spend among campaigns based on performance, and reporting brings results across platforms together. Newer generative features help create and adapt creative assets, with brand controls.

item.title: SocialBee
item.description:
SocialBee organizes posting by category, such as promotions, tips, and behind-the-scenes, so a profile keeps a deliberate mix rather than random posts. Evergreen content can be recycled automatically, and a calendar shows what is scheduled.

AI helps generate posts, captions, and images, and its Copilot suggests a strategy and content plan from a business description. Team features support approvals and client work, and analytics report performance.

SocialBee is paid, with plans by profiles. Alternatives include Buffer, Later, Publer, Hootsuite, and Metricool. SocialBee suits small businesses and agencies.

item.title: Sprout Social
item.description:
Sprout Social is built for teams that manage social media as a function, not a side task. A calendar plans and schedules content across networks such as Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, X, and TikTok, and approval flows keep drafts under review before they go out. A smart inbox gathers messages, comments, and mentions from every channel into one stream that can be assigned, tagged, and replied to by a team.

Analytics are a major selling point. Reports show how posts perform, how audiences grow, and how competitors compare, and they can be exported or shared with clients and executives. Listening tools track brand mentions, topics, and sentiment across social and the web, which helps with crisis monitoring and market research. Influencer marketing and employee advocacy tools extend into related work. AI Assist helps write posts, change tone, and draft replies, and it can summarize sentiment from conversations.

item.title: Stamped.io
item.description:
Stamped helps online stores build trust. After a purchase, it emails customers asking for reviews, collects star ratings with photos or videos, and displays them on product pages and in search results with structured data. Social proof improves conversion rates, and review requests can be automated and timed, with options to send coupons for leaving a review.

The platform also offers loyalty and referral programs. Customers earn points for purchases and actions, redeem rewards, and refer friends, which encourages repeat business. AI features summarize reviews into key themes, surface what customers love or dislike, and help merchants respond. Reports show review volume, ratings, and the effect on sales, and integrations connect with email, helpdesk, and ads tools.

item.title: Surfer SEO
item.description: Surfer helps writers create content that matches what already ranks. You enter a keyword and it analyzes the top search results, then suggests the terms, headings, length, and structure those pages share. As you write in its editor, a content score updates, giving a quick sense of how well your page covers the topic. Writers and SEO teams use it to guide drafts and to update old posts that have dropped in rankings.

item.title: Unbounce AI
item.description:
Unbounce helps marketers create landing pages that convert. A drag-and-drop builder and templates make it possible to publish pages without developers, with popups and sticky bars to capture leads on websites. Marketers connect pages to ad campaigns and test variants to find what performs best.

AI is a core part. Smart Copy generates headlines and body text from a brief, and Smart Traffic uses machine learning to send each visitor to the variant they are most likely to convert on, based on their attributes, which can improve results faster than a standard A/B test. Newer tools analyze pages and suggest improvements, and AI builder features create a page from a prompt.

item.title: Venngage
item.description:
Venngage targets people who need to communicate information visually. Users start from thousands of templates for infographics, reports, flyers, presentations, and social graphics, replace the content, and customize colors, icons, and charts. Data can be imported to generate charts, and the tool includes maps and diagrams for explaining processes and comparisons.

It differentiates itself with business features. Brand kits apply logos, fonts, and colors automatically, team workspaces allow collaboration and approvals, and an accessibility checker flags color contrast and other issues. AI tools generate infographic designs from text, write copy, and suggest improvements, and designs can be exported or shared with analytics.

item.title: WooCommerce
item.description:
WooCommerce is the most widely used way to run a store on WordPress. You install the plugin, add products, set up payments, shipping, and taxes, and manage orders from the WordPress dashboard. Because it is open source, you own the store and the data, host it where you want, and can modify anything with code or extensions.

The ecosystem is its strength. Thousands of themes and extensions add subscriptions, bookings, memberships, marketplaces, and connections to accounting and marketing tools. AI extensions can write product descriptions, suggest recommendations, and help with support, and Automattic’s own tools plus third-party plugins fill the gaps. Many agencies build custom stores on top of it.

item.title: Writesonic
item.description:
Writesonic started as a template-based copywriter and has widened into a content and marketing suite. Users pick a tool for blog articles, ad copy, product descriptions, emails, or social posts, give a brief, and get a draft. A long-form article writer can produce SEO-minded posts from a keyword with outlines and sources, and a chat assistant answers questions and drafts on demand.

Recent additions center on search visibility. Writesonic has tools to see how a brand is mentioned in AI answer engines such as ChatGPT and Perplexity, plus recommendations for improving content. It also offers brand voice settings, an editor with SEO scoring, and integrations with WordPress and other platforms.

item.title: Yotpo
item.description:
Yotpo helps online stores build trust and repeat business. It collects reviews with photos, shows them on product pages and in search, and runs loyalty programs and referral offers. SMS and email tools extend marketing.

AI summarizes reviews into themes, flags issues, and drafts responses, and analytics tie content to conversion. Integrations cover Shopify, BigCommerce, and other platforms.

Yotpo has a free tier and paid plans that scale with orders. Alternatives include Okendo, Judge.me, Stamped.io, Klaviyo, and Trustpilot. Yotpo suits growing online stores.

item.title: ZoomInfo
item.description:
ZoomInfo provides one of the largest databases of business contacts and companies. Sales and marketing teams search by title, industry, company size, location, and technology to build lists, and see verified email addresses, direct phone numbers, org charts, and firmographic details. Intent data shows which companies are researching topics related to a product, helping teams reach out when interest is high.

The platform has expanded from data into a workflow product. It includes tools for sales engagement, marketing advertising, conversation intelligence through Chorus, and enrichment that keeps CRM records up to date automatically. AI features include assistants that research accounts, draft outreach, and recommend who to contact, and agents that handle prospecting tasks. It integrates with Salesforce, HubSpot, and other systems.

item.title: Bloomreach
item.description:
Bloomreach serves online retailers. Its discovery product powers site search, category pages, and recommendations, using machine learning to understand what shoppers mean, rank products, and personalize results. Merchandisers can set rules and see how changes affect sales.

The platform also includes engagement tools. A customer data platform unifies behavior across channels, and marketing automation sends email, SMS, and push messages triggered by actions. Content management supports headless sites. AI assistants help marketers build campaigns and analyze performance.

item.title: Braze
item.description:
Braze helps brands talk to customers on the channels where they spend time. Marketers segment users by behavior, design journeys in a visual canvas, and send messages triggered by actions such as opening an app, abandoning a cart, or reaching a milestone. Real-time data means messages respond to what is happening now.

AI features improve targeting and creation. Predictive models estimate who might churn or buy, optimization chooses the best send time and channel for each person, and generative tools help write subject lines and copy. Analytics measure the effect of campaigns on retention and revenue.

item.title: CleverTap
item.description:
CleverTap serves brands with mobile apps and large user bases. It collects behavioral data such as app opens, purchases, and feature use, builds segments, and lets marketers send push notifications, email, SMS, WhatsApp, and in-app messages. Journeys can be designed visually so that actions trigger the next message.

AI is used for prediction and optimization. Models estimate which users are likely to churn or convert, choose the best time and channel for each message, and recommend products. A proprietary database designed for large volumes of event data keeps analysis fast, and analytics show retention, funnels, and campaign results.

item.title: Constructor
item.description:
Constructor serves online retailers that want search and discovery to drive revenue. Its engine powers site search, category pages, and recommendations, ranking products using both shopper behavior and business goals such as margin or inventory. Merchandisers can steer results with rules while the system learns from clicks and purchases.

Additional tools include product quizzes that guide shoppers to the right item, personalization that adapts to each visitor, and analytics that show how discovery affects sales. Generative AI features allow conversational shopping assistants that answer questions and suggest products.

item.title: Copysmith
item.description:
Copysmith targets online retailers that need lots of product copy. A merchant can generate descriptions for many products from a spreadsheet or catalog, create ad headlines and text, and draft emails and social posts. Bulk generation saves time when a store has hundreds of items.

Integrations connect it to Shopify and Google Ads, so content can flow into the tools where it is used. Team features allow collaboration and approval, and brand settings keep tone consistent. Some tools support SEO optimization by suggesting keywords.

item.title: Iconosquare
item.description:
Iconosquare started as an Instagram analytics tool and expanded to other networks. Social teams connect accounts and see how posts perform, when audiences are active, and how growth compares with competitors. Reports can be exported for clients, which makes it popular with agencies.

Scheduling and planning tools let teams build a content calendar and publish across networks. AI features suggest captions and hashtags, and a listening module monitors mentions and comments. The focus is on analysis that guides what to post, more than on broad community management.

item.title: Insider
item.description:
Insider helps brands treat each visitor differently. It collects behavior data across channels, builds unified profiles, and uses them to personalize websites, app experiences, and messages. A marketer can design a journey that reaches a customer by email, then push, then SMS depending on what they do.

The AI layer predicts what people are likely to buy or whether they may churn, recommends products, and optimizes timing and content. The platform also includes tools for search, recommendations, and conversational commerce. It is used heavily by retailers and consumer brands in many regions.

item.title: Iterable
item.description:
Iterable lets marketers build cross-channel journeys. They segment customers by behavior, design workflows in a visual canvas, and send messages triggered by actions, such as signing up, abandoning a cart, or reaching a milestone. Data from websites, apps, and warehouses feeds the profile used for personalization.

AI assists in several areas: optimizing the time a message is sent for each person, predicting engagement, recommending content, and helping generate copy. Experimentation tools test variants, and analytics tie campaigns to outcomes. Integration with data warehouses supports teams that centralize customer data.

item.title: Klevu
item.description:
Klevu improves how online shoppers find products. Instead of matching keywords exactly, its search engine uses natural language processing to interpret queries, handle synonyms and misspellings, and rank results based on relevance and merchandising goals. It works with platforms such as Shopify, Magento, and BigCommerce.

The product also includes category browsing, recommendations, and analytics on what shoppers search for and fail to find. Merchandisers can adjust results with rules, and AI personalization adapts to a shopper’s behavior. A chat-style assistant answers product questions.

item.title: Latte Social
item.description:
Latte Social covers the basics of content planning. Users connect accounts, ask the AI for post ideas and captions tuned to a brand’s voice, schedule content on a calendar, and publish to several networks. The tool aims to keep a steady posting schedule without constant effort.

For small teams and individual creators, that combination of drafting and scheduling reduces time spent on routine social tasks. AI-generated posts are a starting point and tend to be generic without personal details and specific examples.

item.title: Loomly
item.description:
Loomly supports the planning side of social media. Teams build a content calendar, get post ideas from trends and prompts, draft posts with images and links, and route them through an approval workflow before publishing. A brand asset library keeps logos and images handy.

The platform previews how a post will look on each network and schedules publishing. Analytics show performance, and ad management features support boosted posts. AI assists with captions and ideas.

item.title: Madgicx
item.description:
Madgicx is built for performance marketers and e-commerce brands running paid social. It connects to ad accounts and analyzes campaigns, then recommends or applies changes such as shifting budget toward better-performing ad sets, pausing losers, or testing new audiences. Automation rules run these changes continuously.

Creative tools help with the content side. The platform analyzes which creatives perform best and helps generate variations, and reporting dashboards combine data from ads and online stores into one view. Audience tools find lookalike segments and retargeting groups.

item.title: Mutiny
item.description:
Mutiny changes what a website says depending on the visitor. If a visitor comes from a target account, an industry, or a campaign, Mutiny swaps in headlines, proof points, and calls to action that fit, using firmographic data and ad information. Marketers set this up in a visual editor without developers.

AI recommends segments and generates alternative copy, then tests variations and reports on conversions. Integrations connect with CRMs, ad platforms, and customer data tools so personalization can follow account-based marketing programs.

item.title: Octane AI
item.description:
Octane AI lets stores add an interactive quiz to their site. Shoppers answer questions about preferences, and the quiz recommends products and captures their answers and contact details. Because customers volunteer the information, it is called zero-party data, and it supports personalized email and text marketing.

The platform integrates with Shopify and marketing tools such as Klaviyo, so quiz results can feed segments and flows. Brands use it for skincare, supplements, food, and other categories where choosing among many products is hard. Analytics show how quizzes affect conversion.

item.title: Pallyy
item.description:
Pallyy keeps social management simple and affordable. Users connect accounts, plan posts on a visual calendar, and publish to several networks. A first-comment feature, link-in-bio pages, and a media library support common creator workflows, and a unified inbox collects comments and messages.

Analytics show growth and engagement, and client-friendly reports help agencies prove results. Collaboration tools let clients approve content before it goes live. AI features suggest captions, hashtags, and ideas to speed up planning.

item.title: Publer
item.description:
Publer provides the essentials of social media planning at a modest price. Users connect accounts, build a calendar, schedule posts and recurring content, and see analytics on performance. Bulk scheduling and a library of media help manage volume.

Features include collaboration and approvals, link in bio pages, and a social inbox. The AI assistant writes captions, suggests hashtags, and repurposes content, and tools recycle evergreen posts.

Publer has a free plan with limits and paid tiers by social accounts. Alternatives include Buffer, Later, Metricool, Hootsuite, and Pallyy. Publer suits creators and small teams who want an affordable scheduler.

item.title: Vista Social
item.description:
Vista Social covers social publishing end to end. Teams connect profiles, plan a calendar, schedule content, and respond to comments and messages in one inbox. Approval workflows suit agencies working with clients, and reports summarize performance.

The platform includes reputation management, with review monitoring, and tools for tracking competitors. The AI assistant writes captions, suggests hashtags, and repurposes content. It supports newer networks quickly, which agencies value.

Vista Social has a free plan and paid tiers by profiles and users. Alternatives include Hootsuite, Sprout Social, Buffer, Later, and Agorapulse. Vista Social suits agencies and brands managing many accounts.

item.title: Aiter.io
item.description:
Aiter.io aims at the problem of generic AI marketing copy. A user enters a website address, and the tool reads the site to understand the product, audience, and tone. It then drafts ad variations, social posts, and email campaigns that follow that voice, so small teams can produce material without starting from a blank page.

This kind of tool is meant for founders and small marketing teams who lack time or staff. It can produce a first set of campaign assets quickly, which a person then edits and approves. Output quality depends heavily on how clear the website is, and any generated claim needs checking for accuracy.

item.title: Averi AI
item.description:
Averi is aimed at early-stage companies with big content goals and small teams. It plans topics, drafts articles, and produces supporting copy such as landing pages and social posts, using information about the company’s product and audience to keep content on message.

The idea is to give a founder something like a content department: a planner who chooses what to write, a writer who drafts, and an editor workflow for review. Output is positioned around ranking in search and being cited in AI answers, which are goals that depend on quality and on the site’s authority.

item.title: BlogSEO
item.description:
BlogSEO aims to automate the path from keyword to published post. A user enters a topic or website, the tool finds relevant keywords, creates an outline based on what ranks, and drafts an article. Some workflows can schedule and publish posts directly to a content management system.

For small businesses without a writer, that can mean a steady flow of blog content. The risk is that generic, unedited AI articles rarely rank well and can weaken a site’s credibility. Search engines favor original, helpful pages, so the strongest use is to draft quickly and then add real expertise, examples, and fact-checking.

item.title: Clearscope
item.description: Clearscope helps writers produce content that is complete enough to rank. You enter a keyword, and it analyzes the top results to show the terms, topics, and questions that strong pages tend to include. As you draft in its editor, a grade updates, so you can see whether the page covers what searchers expect. Plugins for Google Docs, Word, and WordPress let writers work in familiar tools instead of switching to a separate app.

item.title: Crayon
item.description:
Crayon helps companies keep an eye on their rivals. It continuously monitors thousands of data points, such as changes to competitors’ web pages, pricing, messaging, reviews, hiring patterns, and press coverage, and alerts the team when something meaningful changes. Instead of manually checking competitor sites, product marketers receive a feed of updates they can review and share.

The platform turns the data into usable materials. Teams build battlecards that give sales reps talking points against each competitor, and distribute them in the CRM or in chat tools such as Slack. Analytics track which competitive content is used in deals, and AI summarizes changes, drafts updates, and filters noise. Win-loss insights connect competitive information to outcomes.

item.title: Pounce
item.description:
Pounce helps with timely engagement. It monitors social platforms for topics and conversations related to a brand or niche, flags those gaining traction, and suggests ways to participate, such as posting a response or creating content.

Social media managers use it to catch trends early, when joining a conversation can earn reach. Faster detection and suggested angles shorten the path from trend to post.

Independent information is limited. Brands should be careful about jumping on trends, as tone-deaf posts cause harm. Pounce has a free tier and paid plans. Alternatives include Brandwatch, Sprout Social listening, Exploding Topics, BuzzSumo, and Google Trends. Pounce suits social managers who want trend alerts.

item.title: Predis.ai
item.description: Predis.ai aims to make social content creation quick for small businesses and creators.
